Q: Can the O(1) property of pop_back() be reused to erase any element of a std::vector? A:

Yes.

You can swap the element you want to erase with the last element, then erase the last element.

This avoids shifting and makes the erase operation constant‑time.

Example :

std::vector<int> vec{1, 2, 4, 3};
auto it = vec.begin() + 1;   // element at index 1
auto last = vec.end() - 1;   // last element
std::iter_swap(it, last);    // swap the two elements
vec.pop_back();              // erase last element (O(1))

After this operation, the vector contains: 1 3 4

Note:

This technique does not preserve the order of elements.

If order matters, you must use the regular erase, which is O(N).

Q: Why is IN(s) much slower than alternatives, especially index(s)? A:

IN(s) is slower because it takes a stream. This means IN($names[]) has to regenerate that entire stream for every element you test, and that repeated work is the bottleneck. By contrast, index(s) works on an array directly in C. It skips the stream overhead entirely.

# slow: stream regenerated for every .name
map(select(.name | IN($names[])))

# fast: array search, no repeated stream
map(select($names | index(.name)))

Even if you try to rewrite IN with first, the stream still gets produced each time. So the gain is modest. Since the built-in any already short-circuits, switching to first doesn't fix the fundamental cost. I don't think jq can optimize IN to match index because stream evaluation is just how that API works. For repeated lookups, I'd build an object once using INDEX to get O(1) performance.

Q: cmake error `No integer type of size 8 was found.` when trying to compile `sundials` A:

Looks like a type in script. If in script code is

set(POSSIBLE_INT64 int64_t;__int64;long long;long)

the correct way is to avoidspace being counted as list separator is to escape it:

set(POSSIBLE_INT64 int64_t;__int64;long\ long;long)

or turn it into a list of quote-wrapped strings

set(POSSIBLE_INT64 "int64_t" "__int64" "long long" "long")

That doesn't mean there is some other error in code too, provided that overriding value of SUNDIALS_INDEX_TYPE. But as override contains space, the line should be

set(POSSIBLE_INT64 "${SUNDIALS_INDEX_TYPE}")

And as comments said that the name should be SUNDIALS_CINDEX_TYPE, that's probably is a typo too.

Q: Clang accepts explicit call to overloaded conversion function while GCC and MSVC rejects A:

The program is well-formed and clang is correct in accepting the program as explained below.

The non-template conversion function is not viable because it is not a const member function while the object s has a top level const. On the other hand, the the tempalated conversion function is marked const and also a candidate for the explicit function call since class.member.lookup-7 states:

If M is a non-dependent conversion-function-id, conversion function templates that are members of T are considered. For each such template F, the lookup set S(t,T) is constructed, considering a function template declaration to have the name t only if it corresponds to a declaration of F ([basic.scope.scope]). The members of the declaration set of each such lookup set, which shall not be an invalid set, are included in the result.

So, the templated version is a candidate. Also it is viable(as it is marked const). Thus, it is the only viable option here. And the call should succeed.

Q: How do I create a table using Pugjs or Jade A:

Your issue has to do with where you're starting your each loop, but there are also some structural issues with your JSON.

I am assuming that you're passing the object into your route like this:

var data = { "accounts": ... }
res.render('templatename', data);

Which means that the accounts object will be at the root of your pug template when it is rendered.

When you create a loop on accounts (an object, not an array) pug will iterate over every property in that object, so your first each (each users in accounts) will give you these two values in the users variable:

  1. user
  2. application

I don't think that's what you want. If you converted the accounts.user segment into an array you could successfully loop through a set of users like this:

each user in accounts.users

As for the second, you will need to reference the application as follows:

each application in accounts.application

Alternatively, you might be passing the data into the render function like this:

var data = { "accounts": ... }
res.render('templatename', data.accounts);

If you do it this way then you will loop through the users like this:

each user in users

The application loop will be this:

each application in applications

Please take a quick look at the pug iteration docs for more reference.
